Developed by: BLACK HOLE STUDIO GOA 19-Year-Old Assagao Fire Victim Succumbs To Injuries While Undergoing Treatment By Team Herald Published: 20 November 2026 Share SHARE ASSAGAO: A 19-year-old youth, identified as Ratnesh Chavan, a native of Uttar Pradesh, succumbed to severe burn injuries while un-dergoing treatment at Goa Medical College (GMC), Bambolim, on November 18. Developed by: BLACK HOLE STUDIO GOA Jesuit priest, educationist Fr Apollo Cardozo laid to rest By Team Herald Published: 20 November 2026 Share SHARE MARGAO: Jesuit priest, educationist and writer Fr Apolinario (Apollo) Cardozo, SJ, who passed away on Wednesday following a brief illness, was laid to rest at the Pedro Arrupe Institute, Raia, on Thursday. The mortal remains of Fr Apollo were brought to the Basilica of Bom Jesus, Old Goa, at 1 pm for people to pay their final respects, followed by a funeral Mass at 3 pm.

Developed by: BLACK HOLE STUDIO GOA FTII professor urges young filmmakers to tap Konkani literature Calls on young creators to turn Konkani stories into films, stressing that compelling ideas matter more than big budgets By Team Herald Published: 20 November 2026 Share SHARE SHASHWAT GUPTA RAY PANJIM: Goa’s rich literary tradition could provide the foundation for a new generation of filmmakers, but aspiring creators must be willing to move beyond the constraints of conventional filmmaking and turn their ideas into films using the technology readily available to them, Professor of Screen Studies at the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, Indranil Bhattacharya, has said.

items.title: Kanhangad and Kochi
items.hook: Konkani families settled far down the coast.
paras: Konkani-speaking families settled in Kanhangad in northern Kerala and in Kochi over centuries, and their temples and community institutions are still active.
These communities keep the language alive well outside Goa and Karnataka.
items.wow: Konkani is spoken in four states today because of centuries of coastal trade and migration.

items.title: Shri Chitrapur Math, Shirali
items.hook: The spiritual home of the Chitrapur Saraswat community, in Uttara Kannada.
paras: The Shri Chitrapur Math is the math of the Chitrapur Saraswat Brahmin community, with its headquarters at Shirali in Karnataka.
It has guided the community's religious and cultural life for generations, and runs schools, hostels and charitable work alongside its spiritual role.
items.wow: Chitrapur Saraswats are spread across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Goa and overseas, but Shirali remains the centre.

items.title: Shrimad Partagali Jeevottam Math
items.hook: The Gaud Saraswat math at Partagali in Canacona, south Goa.
paras: The Shrimad Partagali Jeevottam Math is one of the principal maths of the Gaud Saraswat Brahmin community.
It is named after Shrimad Jeevottam Teerth, and its annual festivals draw GSB families from Goa, Karnataka and Maharashtra.
items.wow: The Gaud Saraswat community is often called the GSB, and its maths in Goa and at Kashi are both central to its identity.

items.title: Shri Kashi Math Samsthan
items.hook: A coastal community's math, far away in Varanasi.
paras: The Shri Kashi Math Samsthan is a math of the Gaud Saraswat Brahmin community with its headquarters at Varanasi.
Its branches and followers are spread through coastal Karnataka, Goa, Kerala and Maharashtra, and its swamijis travel to the community's centres through the year.
items.wow: For a coastal community, having its math in Kashi is a reminder of how far Saraswat families travelled for scholarship.

items.title: Shri Shantadurga Temple, Kavlem
items.hook: The goddess of peace, at Ponda in Goa.
paras: The Shri Shantadurga temple at Kavlem in Ponda is one of the most visited temples of the Gaud Saraswat community.
The name means the goddess of peace, and the temple's annual jatra is a major event in Goa.
items.wow: Several Goan temples, including this one, were moved inland in the 16th century to keep them safe.
